fact: Low-value transactions within the Common Monetary Area (Eswatini, South Africa, Lesotho, Namibia) are migrating from domestic electronic funds transfer rails to the Transactions Cleared on an Immediate Basis payment scheme, per ITWeb Africa.

fact: The South African Reserve Bank directive says low-value cross-border electronic funds transfers within the Common Monetary Area (Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia, South Africa) are currently executed through SADC-RTGS.

The South African Reserve Bank directive says Common Monetary Area low-value transfers, including this country's, run through the SADC-RTGS regional system and must move to the TCIB scheme by April 2027.
The directive says low-value cross-border electronic funds transfers within the Common Monetary Area are currently executed through SADC-RTGS.

The CMA Cross-border Payments Oversight Committee's paper of 31 July 2024 says rand cross-border low-value EFTs within the Common Monetary Area, including Eswatini, run through an interim supplementary-file solution in place since 1 October 2019 and still in use.

The CMA committee's paper of 31 July 2024 says banks route low-value cross-border EFTs within the CMA, Eswatini among its four members, through the SADC real-time gross settlement system under the interim arrangement, to move to a designated retail system such as TCIB from 1 April 2027.
